meta.storyTitle: Isolate each code and design review in its own worker thread

summary.prose: Each code or design review runs in a dedicated daemon-owned worker, independent of chat-session threads and other reviews. Submission is durably acknowledged before expensive scope/subject admission, with progress and technical failures visible throughout. Existing review coordinators, judging policies, trusted controller ownership and human approval gates remain authoritative; this change relocates execution and adds the missing admission lifecycle.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: Standalone feature — no parent HLD. Design directly against the repo, grounded on the s1 analyze passes. There are no HLD shared contracts to honour.

boundary.internal: Isolate each code and design review in its own worker thread

errors.condition: Malformed/oversized request, unregistered/noncanonical repo, wrong owner, conflicting review identity or worker boot/persistence failure before durable acknowledgment.

preconditions: Approved source route and author-party checks are preserved, with authority determined by host data rather than caller claims.
Main registry reserves canonical repo + review family + reviewId; both review families also retain existing subject/cleanup exclusions.
postconditions: Expensive committed-source reads/projection and all coordinator execution occur on the dedicated review worker.
No model call is dispatched before full source/route admission succeeds.
Daemon review remains live after submitter disconnect; controller-review owner disconnect retains existing explicit recovery requirements.

preconditions: Artifact subject resolves to registered repo and host-authorized path; design artifact lease remains process-wide despite moving coordinator state into workers.
Main bridge validates connection identity and action envelope; workers cannot mint caller authority.

Existing latest-artifact monitoring, user-directed restart policy and bounded technical retries remain unchanged.
Code and design review method routes cannot silently fall back to main/session execution, including when optional session threading is disabled.

dataModelChanges.details: Proposed src/daemon/threads/review-workers.ts and src/daemon/threads/review-worker.ts host one existing family coordinator per canonical (repo,family,reviewId). Reuse startWorker, workerScript, startDaemonWorker, HubClient, serveRequests, status-board and supervisor hooks. The registry owns 0..N active worker entries; each active entry owns exactly one worker and one review identity; a worker owns exactly one review, never a pool or a session. An attempt sequence reuses its live owner; after termination, explicit resume/recover/publication retry may spawn a replacement only after the prior worker is gone and its resources are reclaimed. Main registry entries hold threadId, worker incarnation, family, repo, reviewId, attempt, subject/cleanup scope, trusted owner bridge, last published bounded progress and reclaimed promise. These are process-lifetime routing facts, not a second durable review ledger. Use a worker incarnation tied to the registered MessagePort to reject stale exit/progress/result messages; clients cannot supply it. Do not use startClassWorker's singleton class target for per-review routing. Add a review role/identity to existing thread registry/status types where needed, and carry existing session attribution for diagnostics without attaching the worker lifetime to the chat worker. Relationship table (authoritative cardinalities): registry -> active worker entries 0..N; active worker -> review identity exactly 1; review identity -> active worker 0..1; review identity -> trusted controller owner 0..1; controller owner -> owned review identities 0..N; persisted review identity -> checkpoint attempts 1..N; attempt -> review identity exactly 1. Worker/owner references are optional for stored and daemon-reviewed identities; removing a runtime worker never deletes the durable identity. This explicit table replaces the ER companion because the current LinkML renderer cannot express the required inverse cardinalities faithfully.

Extend each family's checkpoint attempt contract with an explicit admission variant rather than creating sidecar packet files or a second authoritative store. Existing admitted attempts retain their current submitted/review-response form and immutable history; historical current-format checkpoints remain readable without rewriting their reviewed content. An admission variant contains the existing immutable submitted input once, attempt number/review identity, operation/action identity, acceptedAt, status pending|running|failed|interrupted, bounded progress, source-validation state unverified, and optional typed technical error. Task/chunk selection and source fingerprints are absent until actually established; absence is not empty successful scope. It cannot carry review findings, a passing verdict, accepted scope or an approval binding. Worker saves this variant atomically before acknowledgment, then qualifies route, pins, source history, subject and capacity using current checks. On success atomically replace the same current attempt with the ordinary admitted variant, transferring the same submitted input and retaining admission timing; only then permit provider work. On failure retain the admission variant and exact input with a bounded code/field/summary. Readers, recovery, capacity and cleanup must discriminate both variants before accessing task/chunk fields. The schema/version gate must advertise the new format; updated readers accept existing qualified history, while an older binary must refuse unsupported admission variants rather than misread them as successful review. Failed admission consumes its attempt identity: corrected inputs require the next explicit attempt; identical interrupted admission resumes only via existing explicit resume/recover semantics. No automatic inference retry and no same-attempt input replacement. Durable resource guard: each attempt additionally retains a bounded mutable resourceGuard:{daemonInstance, openLeases:[{operationId,workerIncarnation,kind,openedAt}], clearance?:{at,reason,approvalReceipt:{requestId,decision:'approve',reviewKey,guardDigest,leaseIds}}} in the SAME family checkpoint. It is native-lifetime metadata, not another review ledger, not a transcript and not a list of all finished commands. Remove an open lease only after positively confirmed disposal; input pins and completed feedback remain immutable. Resource updates share the family's single serialized checkpoint-save path so progress/results cannot overwrite a newly opened lease. Enforce existing checkpoint size/count limits before reserving/starting a command; never drop an unresolved lease to fit the limit.
dataModelChanges.schemaDiff: CheckpointAttempt = AdmissionAttempt | ExistingQualifiedAttempt; AdmissionAttempt.phase='admission'; validation='unverified'; submitted remains exact and bounded. Only ExistingQualifiedAttempt may own accepted task/chunk scope, finalScope identity or BUILD/artifact approval binding. Format capability/version must be updated in registered schema and readers.

dataModelChanges.details: Sequence: caller -> main existing MCP/RPC adapter -> cheap canonical identity/size/trusted-owner validation and atomic in-memory review reservation -> start one registered worker -> worker structural validation and atomic admission-checkpoint save -> durable-submission acknowledgment -> worker expensive admission -> ordinary qualified checkpoint -> existing family execution -> publication -> bounded final progress -> worker drain/reclaim. Failure before durable save is returned synchronously and releases reservation after worker exit; no acknowledgment is claimed. Response loss after save is discoverable by progress and identical submission replay returns the existing acknowledgment without rerunning work; changed payload for the same pinned attempt is rejected. Observation by another session does not steal controller authority. Main can serve cached worker progress during expensive admission; cache is a bounded projection of durable state with freshness/time and must not fabricate progress. Existing startWorker has no readiness deadline. Add a parent-owned 30-second bootstrap deadline, starting before worker creation and ending only after worker-ready AND confirmed durable admission-save acknowledgment. It is a local startup/save bound, never a review/admission/model deadline. Expiry targets that worker only: mark its incarnation closing, deny new child requests, reject late readiness/save replies as acknowledgments, return review-worker-bootstrap-timeout promptly and initiate targeted stop/reclamation in the background. Keep that identity fenced until child disposal and lock/store reclamation are confirmed; only then release its reservation. If a late atomic save exists, retain it as an interrupted submission discoverable by progress; never overwrite it or silently replay. If cleanup cannot be proven, retain only that identity's resource fence and report recovery-required. No silent main-thread fallback. Reuse scope_preparation/task-null for code admission progress; map design admission to an explicit pre-plan state in its reader contract. Clients must display pending admission and distinguish it from completed empty scope. Progress DTO clarification: reuse code phase scope_preparation with task:null and numeric totalTasks:0 until qualified task inventory is established; zero here means not yet known while status is pending/running and admission.validation is unverified, never successful empty scope. Add optional admission:{state:pending|validating|failed|interrupted,validation:'unverified',stage,acceptedAt,error?:{code,field?,summary}} to both acknowledgment/progress readers. Design uses phase admission and totalChunks:0 before accepted plan, with the same explicit unverified state. After qualification, existing task/chunk progress applies and totals reflect actual inventory. IDE fixtures/renderers display 'Preparing review' rather than '0 tasks completed'; terminal admission failure is displayed as technical failure, not findings.

dataModelChanges.entity: Trusted controller and tool context bridge
dataModelChanges.details: Keep host connection authority and controller action validation in main-daemon entrypoints. AbortSignal, closures, providers and live sockets are not structured-cloned. Main creates an internal owner handle bound to authenticated connection identity and registered worker port; worker reconstructs a local AbortController from explicit owner-loss/cancellation notifications. Carry only bounded serializable client/model context and existing action/execution/sequence envelopes. Use existing nested routing for daemon-owned services, approved tool execution and permission requests; worker tools preserve existing checks, callbacks and source provenance. A review worker may receive only its own review's exchanges; verify repo/family/reviewId/attempt, worker incarnation and controller owner before forwarding. Untrusted fields cannot impersonate a controller or choose reviewer party. Controller disconnect interrupts only that review according to current protocol; daemon-authored/background reviewer execution survives observer disconnect. Main keeps durable subject/cleanup authority coherent across review workers; global design-artifact leases cannot remain worker-local module globals. Use existing review-state/host ownership services for cross-worker fencing, not new user trust keys. For resource clearance, reuse the existing local-client authorization model and approval broker; do not authenticate human responders or add answering-channel eligibility. A normal accepted broker decision may come from a human UI or an automated local client. Main binds its requestId to the exact canonical review, unresolved-resource digest and lease set; an approval supplied as a worker field or caller-asserted receipt is not a broker outcome. Resource clearance is separate from artifact signoff and does not grant BUILD/LLD approval. Existing trusted-controller identity and cross-worker action checks elsewhere in this bridge remain unchanged.

Preserve existing task/chunk semantics and permanent CR/design report history. Technical admission failure is rendered as admission failure with no model/task/chunk verdict; add a bounded explicitly non-review admission-failure history section to the existing report contracts where needed so next attempts can retain it without manufacturing task results. Only admitted whole-story/current-artifact independent passing evidence can satisfy approval. Failed admission never binds BUILD or invalidates a prior approval as newly reviewed content. Progress/read-only history remain accessible after worker exit from atomic checkpoints/permanent reports; readers discriminate admission variants without rerunning Git qualification. Publication retries start a dedicated recovery worker if necessary, consume durable feedback only and do not redispatch models. Cleanup after successful approval first fences the specific existing story/artifact scope across workers, drains or refuses active admission/execution/publication, then uses existing evidence-preserving deletion rules in a dedicated worker; never broad-delete other review files. Historical retry/approval paths that currently requalify checkpoints synchronously must route the costly work to that worker too. An already-published review read should not spawn a provider. Add tests for failed admission -> successful next attempt -> permanent publication -> human approval cleanup -> post-cleanup read for BOTH families; technical diagnostics survive in permanent history without becoming review findings or changing earlier approval evidence. Publication retries after lost receipts/worker exit must assert zero provider calls through real routing.

Add a main-daemon-owned review child-process lease service alongside the worker registry (proposed src/daemon/threads/review-processes.ts); worker death must not own the only cancellation handle. Review computation, model routing, structured-output parsing, tool-output parsing and checkpoints stay in its review worker. Only native process creation, bounded byte transport and lifecycle disposal run in the main host. Reuse the subprocess lifecycle implementations in src/shared/process-group.ts (CliProvider) and src/daemon/tools/shell-helper.ts (Git/tools), with a narrowly scoped injectable bridge installed for review-worker execution. Route ALL worker-originated native commands through that bridge, including admission Git commands, CLI provider sessions, managed tool shell calls and streamed/raw-byte subprocess paths; test an inventory of review-reachable spawn sites and refuse any unbridged native spawn on a review worker. Other non-review callers retain their current execution paths. Do not repurpose src/native/process-broker, whose current command allowlist is daemon-only, or invent claims that StartedWorker.reclaimed disposes child processes.

Each command request is bound to canonical review key + registered worker incarnation/port + unique operationId. Main validates the authorized argv/cwd/tool context through existing permission/provenance checks, creates the lease and its host AbortController BEFORE invoking a spawn-capable helper, and keeps the spawn/registration transition synchronous with respect to worker-exit notifications (no await between lease creation and invoking the helper). If the worker/lease is already closing, refuse before spawn; if it exits during creation, the host-owned abort is already registered and owns disposal. A duplicate operationId with identical input observes that lease, never spawns again; conflicting replay is rejected. The worker receives only serializable output/exit events and local cancellation handles, never a ChildProcess object. Existing activity stream consumption receives bounded chunks with backpressure; parsing remains in the worker. Worker exit rejects outstanding output-consumption replies and aborts every lease for that incarnation, so a dead worker cannot keep the host waiting for output acknowledgment.

Host uses the existing managed process-group cleanup, extends its result to distinguish confirmed close/disposal from kill requested/settlement timeout/unknown, and retains cancellation and exit observation outside the worker. A helper's settlement timeout or a sent signal is NOT disposal evidence. Disposal completes only after owned child close/exit plus the helper's verified owned-group cleanup outcome; permission errors, unknown group state or unclosed descendants retain the targeted resource fence and explicit recovery-required error. Do not kill arbitrary PIDs or use the daemon-only native broker as a generic child terminator. No replacement review worker may dispatch a provider until the old incarnation's command leases are confirmed disposed AND StartedWorker.reclaimed confirms locks/stores. This closes crash-before-spawn, crash-during-spawn and crash-after-spawn registration races without a second review ledger or globally serializing reviews.

Normal terminal execution drains checkpoint/publication saves, host process leases, then worker exit/reclamation before registry release. Unexpected worker death marks only that review interrupted; exact atomic checkpoint and completed feedback remain. Explicit resume/recover creates one replacement after disposal/reclamation; no fabricated family results. Daemon shutdown aborts/drains host-owned leases before terminating workers; after a full daemon crash, unknown previous child disposal must remain an explicit targeted recovery fence until established, never guessed from PID absence alone. Required review workers operate even when optional session routing is disabled. Worker/resource failures are explicit; no global pool, activation flag or fallback engine.

FULL DAEMON LOSS: main-memory lease ownership alone is insufficient. Use this order for every native command: worker requests a main-host lease reservation; worker durably saves that lease as open in its current checkpoint through the existing serialized writer; only then may the main-host lease service start the command, after checking that the same registered incarnation/reservation is still live. Host must reject a start without that durable-intent receipt. Main's reserved lease exists before any spawn, so worker loss between reservation and persistence starts nothing; worker loss after persistence but before spawn can leave a conservative open intent, never an unrecorded child. On confirmed child/group disposal, host reports closure and the worker durably removes the lease; a failure to persist closure remains conservatively open. An open intent may therefore mean either potentially live native work or completed work lacking a saved closure; both are fenced after full-daemon loss.

Restart discovery is REQUEST-SCOPED: on explicit start/resume/recover/publication/cleanup for a saved review, read its bounded resourceGuard before launching a new worker or native command. An open lease from another daemon instance, or an interrupted legacy active attempt with no resource guard, reconstructs an in-memory resource fence for exactly that canonical review identity. A missing live registry entry, missing PID, identical command name or an old worker exit is NOT clearance evidence. Do not scan/resume all saved reviews at daemon startup. Unrelated review identities remain usable; only the affected identity cannot dispatch native work. Expose resource-recovery-required with the saved lease IDs/instance/time, not credentials or raw command output.

CLEARANCE — EXISTING LOCAL TRUST: while the original host is alive, retained exact child ownership and confirmed disposal can clear its own lease. Across full-daemon loss, resourceClearance is an explicit local-operator recovery action under the daemon's EXISTING local-client trust model. Its reason asserts that the prior native work was checked/ended; this is operator attestation, not independently measured OS disposal proof. Keep the existing approval broker and approval.answer contracts unchanged: the broker does not distinguish a human UI from an automated local client, and either can answer a normal pending request. No human-only provenance, responder authentication, new trust key, answering-channel eligibility or changes to broker/client authentication are required.

A resourceClearance request on existing code resume/design recover paths names the canonical review identity, affected lease IDs, reason and expected digest of ALL unresolved resourceGuard entries across retained attempts for that identity. Main first validates the normal recovery caller/owner rules, reserves that exact identity, and creates a normal broker request whose pending host state binds requestId to reviewKey, expected guard digest and exact lease set. Only a real accepted approve outcome for this pending request can authorize the metadata update. Missing client, decline, expiry, disconnect, unknown/replayed requestId, changed guard digest or wrong review/lease set leaves the fence in place. A valid automated local answer is permitted under the existing trust model; the design makes no stronger identity claim. A caller boolean, worker actor or fabricated approvalReceipt field cannot replace the broker outcome. Main rechecks the unresolved guard set before persisting the result, so an intervening lease change invalidates the old approval.

Persist a bounded approvalReceipt:{requestId,decision:'approve',at,reviewKey,guardDigest,leaseIds,reason} and closure of only the approved unresolved lease set through one metadata-only recovery worker before releasing the fence. That worker may do filesystem checkpoint work but cannot spawn native commands/providers or become a second execution owner. Persist the clearance idempotently through the existing serialized writer; after response loss, replay observes the stored receipt without another clearance or inference. If a pending broker request is lost on daemon restart, the unchanged fence requires a fresh explicit clearance request. Normal artifact approval never substitutes for this recovery action. Clearance preserves failed/interrupted attempts and prior approval evidence; it cannot authorize model dispatch by itself. Return clearance-complete/recovery-required, and require a subsequent explicit resume/recover for actual review work under existing attempt/pin rules. If native work cannot be confirmed ended, decline clearance and keep the targeted fence; never infer disposal from PID absence or automatically clear on timeout. No global review blocking, automatic restart or arbitrary PID kill is introduced. The native-spawn inventory explicitly includes CliProvider.resolveBin's synchronous execFileSync('which', ...) path: supply host-resolved binary paths or an asynchronous bridged resolution before execution, so a review worker never runs this synchronous subprocess. Include raw byte/stream helpers and any direct spawn/exec sites reachable from review adapters; unknown unbridged sites fail the inventory test.

Proposed new runtime files are src/daemon/threads/review-workers.ts (owner registry/dispatch) and src/daemon/threads/review-worker.ts (single-review worker entrypoint); add focused tests under src/daemon/threads/__tests__. Adapt existing main review RPC adapters, router/method classification/supervisor/status types, family checkpoint/admission/read/publication/cleanup contracts and MCP progress readers/schemas as required. Test families remain existing code/design modules, not a third engine. Live VS Code and JetBrains clients must tolerate/render admission progress and preserve IPC method names/payload identities if shared DTOs change; no deprecated insrc-ide work. No token-accounting code, review judgment algorithm changes, timeout expansion, projection budget increases/optimization, or automatic restarting of another session's reviews. The current TU1 S1 64MiB failure still requires a separately bounded valid scope/implementation correction; worker isolation makes it visible rather than fixing that limit. Correction-round QA evidence is kept only in /tmp: generated sequence/component companions render through headless Chrome using the local offline HTML paths; raw browser DOM and screenshots are available as /tmp/review-worker-sequence-dom.html, /tmp/review-worker-sequence.png, /tmp/review-worker-components-dom.html and /tmp/review-worker-components.png. The reviewer can inspect those independently and may rerun the local headless command; tool unavailability must remain an honest limitation rather than a finding. The obsolete ER companion is removed; the relationship table above is authoritative.

errorCases.scenario: Malformed, oversized, wrong-repository or forged-owner submission
errorCases.detection: Existing schema/size guards plus canonical repo and trusted host identity checks fail before worker dispatch or worker durable save.
errorCases.response: Return existing typed refusal; do not claim durable acceptance, start a provider or create an approval binding. Reclaim any failed bootstrap worker before release.
errorCases.userImpact: Actionable refusal without hidden review work.

errorCases.scenario: Worker cannot boot or admission checkpoint cannot be saved
errorCases.detection: Worker startup error/exit, the parent-owned 30-second ready-plus-durable-save deadline, or rejected atomic checkpoint write before acknowledged persistence.
errorCases.response: Return worker-start/admission-storage/bootstrap-timeout promptly. Deny late readiness/save acknowledgments for the closing incarnation, retain any late durable input as interrupted and start targeted cleanup. Keep only that identity fenced until host child leases and worker locks/stores are reclaimed; never wait indefinitely on cleanup inside the request or fall back to main/session review execution.
errorCases.userImpact: Submission is not accepted; explicit retry is safe after cause is corrected.

errorCases.scenario: Expensive admission rejects pins, source projection, subject or capacity after acknowledgment
errorCases.detection: Existing family qualification checks throw; including current projection decoded-byte/operation limits.
errorCases.response: Persist terminal admission failure with exact immutable request and bounded diagnostic; no provider dispatch and no synthetic task/chunk result. Progress/read/report clearly identifies technical admission failure. A changed input needs a new explicit sequential attempt.
errorCases.userImpact: Failure remains discoverable after MCP return; scope is not silently weakened.

errorCases.detection: Main reservation and saved attempt identity/digest distinguish identical replay, conflicting same-attempt input and genuinely active work.
errorCases.response: Identical acknowledged request returns existing submission identity without restarting work; conflicting payload is refused. Existing same-review exclusion remains, independently of other review IDs.
errorCases.userImpact: No duplicate model calls or accidental overwrite after reconnect.

errorCases.scenario: Review worker crashes while admission, execution or publication is active
errorCases.detection: Main-host registered worker exit/error plus incarnation check; every native command has a main-owned lease created before spawn, with host cancellation and verified disposal state independent of the worker.
errorCases.response: Report only that review interrupted from the main progress projection; preserve last checkpoint and published history. Require explicit resume/recover. Do not create replacement or dispatch models before old worker and children are fenced/reclaimed; never synthesize success. On worker loss, reject pending stream-consumer acknowledgments and abort host-owned command leases. A sent signal or helper settlement timeout is not proof of disposal; retain a targeted recovery fence on unknown cleanup.
errorCases.userImpact: Other reviews and chat sessions continue; completed feedback is retained.

errorCases.scenario: Controller disconnect, forged exchange or stale worker message
errorCases.detection: Main-owned connection lifecycle, owner-bound action envelope and registered worker port/incarnation mismatch.
errorCases.response: Forward loss only to the owning controller review under existing recovery rules; reject forged/stale messages before they mutate checkpoint/status. Daemon reviewer does not inherit observer-disconnect cancellation.
errorCases.userImpact: Authority and independent reviewer semantics survive the thread move.

errorCases.detection: Main cross-worker story/artifact lease and existing evidence-preserving cleanup guard observe a live owner or unresolved worker reclamation.
errorCases.response: Return targeted busy/retained result; do not delete active checkpoint. Retry cleanup after target is inactive; unrelated workers do not receive cancellation.
errorCases.userImpact: No loss of current review evidence or interference with another session.

errorCases.scenario: Unsupported admission format encountered by reader, recovery or older daemon
errorCases.detection: Checkpoint variant/version capability gate cannot decode admission or qualified attempt safely.
errorCases.response: Return explicit unsupported-format error and preserve bytes; no blind downgrade, successful-empty interpretation or automatic history rewrite.
errorCases.userImpact: Operator can upgrade/recover without losing evidence.

errorCases.scenario: Full daemon loss leaves native work with no surviving host handles
errorCases.detection: On an explicit request for one review, its saved resourceGuard has unresolved leases from another daemon instance, or legacy interrupted active work has no disposal record.
errorCases.response: Reconstruct only that review's resource fence before native spawn. Clear with retained exact host disposal proof, or with an explicit local-operator clearance using the EXISTING broker decision model, where human and automated local clients may answer alike. Main binds the pending request to canonical review, digest of all unresolved retained-attempt guards and exact affected leases; recheck before persisting the bounded approval receipt and closures through a metadata-only worker. Fabricated receipts, stale/wrong review/lease sets, decline/expiry/no-client and PID absence cannot clear it. Subsequent explicit resume remains separate; no new human-only authentication promise.
errorCases.userImpact: Potential orphaned work cannot overlap replacement execution without explicit operator attestation under the existing local trust model; unrelated reviews stay available. This does not independently prove the operator's observation.

edgeCases.input: Code/code, design/design or mixed code/design reviews in different sessions, including two from one session
edgeCases.expected: Distinct valid review identities run on distinct worker threadIds, with independent admission/progress and provider lifetimes; existing same-artifact design exclusion still applies.
Reviews still require dedicated worker execution; initialize required safe worker services or return explicit unavailable, never execute heavy work on main.

edgeCases.input: Progress query during a deliberately blocked admission computation
edgeCases.expected: Return pending scope preparation, task null, timestamps/freshness and no invented total; unrelated review and daemon status calls complete without waiting for admission.

edgeCases.input: Existing qualified checkpoint from before this change
edgeCases.expected: Updated readers accept it unchanged; explicit recovery runs in a dedicated worker. Historical review inputs, findings and source pins remain immutable.

edgeCases.input: Worker exits after checkpoint save but before caller receives acknowledgment
edgeCases.expected: Progress/retry discovers the durable admission; identical replay does not dispatch another inference. Recovery is explicit if owner died.

edgeCases.input: Publication fails after all task/chunk results were durably recorded
edgeCases.expected: Retain pending publication and feedback; explicit publication retry runs in one recovery worker without models.

invariantsToPreserve.text: Code-review final source pin and changed-block scope verification, checkpoint input immutability and independent party selection remain mandatory; admission status cannot satisfy BUILD approval.
Design latest-subject monitoring, user-directed artifact-change restart, impact-aware corrections and bounded technical retry behavior remain in the existing coordinator.
Workers are daemon-owned, join shared store/lock guards and reclaim resources on exit; IPC clients never directly open daemon stores.
Controller identity comes from trusted host context and observing a review does not transfer ownership; only targeted controller loss changes its review lifecycle.
Existing family progress/checkpoint recovery tests remain applicable; cross-worker movement must preserve saved partial feedback and explicit recovery.

testStrategy.testFramework: node:test with node:assert/strict, executed by Node 22.22.1 and tsx; extend the existing daemon-thread and code/design-review test suites. Actual worker-thread fixtures with deterministic barriers and stubbed providers; no cloud calls for regression tests.

testLevels.purpose: Prove exact review ownership, input pinning and schema discrimination without provider dispatch.
subjects: Proposed src/daemon/threads/__tests__/review-workers.test.ts: reserve one canonical repo/family/reviewId, distinct worker incarnations and correct subject/cleanup exclusions; reject stale-port and forged-owner exchanges.

Extend family checkpoint/admission/capacity tests: durable admission variant cannot be read as qualified scope, cannot pass approval, retains exact input, fails safely at unchanged projection bounds, and round-trips historical qualified checkpoints.

Native-spawn inventory includes CliProvider.resolveBin execFileSync('which', ...), runInProcessGroup, runShell/runShellBytes/spawnManaged and review-reachable direct spawn/exec sites; review workers cannot bypass the host bridge.
fixturesNeeded: Small pinned review packets and design artifact subjects from existing fixtures.
Admission-phase, failed-admission, interrupted-admission and current qualified-history fixtures; no raw prompt transcripts.

testLevels.purpose: Demonstrate actual isolation and acknowledgment ordering using real worker threads, not only mocked callbacks.
subjects: Proposed src/daemon/threads/__tests__/review-worker-isolation.test.ts: block review A's expensive admission inside its worker after durable acknowledgment; before releasing its barrier, prove daemon status/progress and review B execute on different threadIds.
Run code/code, design/design and code/design permutations from different sessions and from the same session; same-subject exclusion is tested independently of valid parallel reviews.
Prove accepted response follows atomic admission save but precedes expensive source/subject work; progress has scope_preparation/task-null and does not claim total or passing verdict.

Exercise existing start/resume/recover/progress/controller-exchange/publication/cleanup entrypoints through real MCP-step/RPC routing; assert no old main-thread-only route remains and threads-disabled optional session mode never causes fallback.

Real-worker bootstrap fixture never sends ready, and another hangs before durable-save acknowledgment: parent returns named failure within the bootstrap bound, rejects late replies and keeps only the closing identity fenced until reclaimed.
fixturesNeeded: Real compiled worker entrypoint, existing channel/store-guard/lock fixtures, isolated temporary repo/checkpoints.
Worker admission barrier/CPU-block probe and parent-side acknowledgment ordering assertions; generous outer test timeout used only as a test failure guard.

testLevels.purpose: Preserve failure, cancellation, cleanup, trusted authority and restart semantics across workers.
subjects: Proposed src/daemon/threads/__tests__/review-worker-recovery.test.ts: crash before durable save, after save before ack, during qualified task/chunk execution and during publication; prove targeted interruption, saved feedback retention and explicit replacement after reclamation.
Owner disconnect interrupts controller review only; daemon review survives observer disconnect; forged and delayed old-worker messages cannot mutate the replacement.

Same-input replay after lost ack never duplicates dispatch; changed input in pinned attempt is refused; failed admission proceeds only on explicit next attempt, interrupted identical admission on explicit recovery.
Prove provider/tool child release and lock/store reclamation before replacement dispatch; same-scope approval cleanup refuses active work while unrelated reviews stay alive.
Existing code/design ownership, checkpoint, progress, recovery, publication and completion-gate regressions continue to pass.

Crash a worker immediately before a native command request, during host spawn-registration and after child start: all paths have a main-host lease, no orphan provider is left and replacement provider count stays zero until confirmed disposal. Exercise CLI, Git/shell bytes, stream backpressure and late output replies; unbridged review-worker spawn must be refused.

Failed admission followed by successful next attempt, permanent publication, approval cleanup and post-cleanup read preserves technical diagnostics for both families without fabricating findings. Publication retry with lost receipt and after worker exit proves providerCalls===0.
